strongest_angle: Theoretical quantum research by Angelo Esposito, Alberto Nicolis, and Federico Piazza demonstrates that 100 percent transparency is physically impossible because photons inevitably decay into phonons inside any material with a nontrivial index of refraction.

key_facts.fact: Theoretical physicists Angelo Esposito, Alberto Nicolis, and Federico Piazza published research on arXiv in 2026 showing that quantum decay of photons into phonons causes light attenuation in any material with a nontrivial index of refraction, even at 0 kelvin.
Author Matthew von Hippel and editor Clara Moskowitz reported in Scientific American in November 2026 that quantum limits prevent any material from achieving 100 percent optical transparency.
Mikael Rechtsman at Pennsylvania State University conducted experiments on stealthy hyperuniform materials to measure how structural disorder affects photon scattering across band linewidths.
Researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China and Peking University achieved coherent perfect absorption of light within a synthetic photon-phonon lattice in August 2026.
